subject: Streaming session resilience plan & immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia@pulsehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Intermittent streaming disconnects causing retry storms

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a repeat incident this morning where long-running chat sessions against the Redwood API are disconnecting after ~45–60s of inactivity on the client. When clients retry automatically we get a very short window of 429 spikes followed by a burst of 5xx errors (502/503) as the backend overloads. This is causing user-visible interruptions in our clinical workflows and a sharp uptick in token usage.

I've attached a trimmed set of logs and a screenshot showing the 429 spike. Key notes from our SRE:
- Idle disconnects appear to correlate with session durations ~> 180s but idle >45s before next chunk.
- Retrying clients are not applying exponential backoff uniformly.
- Problem first appeared yesterday after a model rollout; we rolled back the model yesterday afternoon with no improvement.

Can you please advise immediate mitigations? We need a short-term fix (hours) and a recovery plan. This is impacting three production customers right now.

Thanks,
Amelia Torres
Director, Integrations — PulseHealth

Attachments: pulsehealth-logs-20270521.tar.gz, screenshot-429spikes.png

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 18:27:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming disconnects causing retry storms

Thanks for the quick report, Amelia — sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as P1 and standing up an incident channel. I've looped in Priyom (SRE/drivers) and Aditya (runtime) to propose immediate mitigations.

Short ask for your SRE team if possible: please forward a sample of the raw client reconnect headers (Authorization mask ok) and the exact retry logic clients use when they re-open the stream. That will help us differentiate client-side vs server-side timeouts.

Immediate next steps from us (I'll summarize in the incident Slack):
- Priyom: propose short-term server-side keepalive / ping to keep streams active for 90s.
- Aditya: evaluate lowering tokenization cost by routing to a lower-throughput model variant for reopened streams.
- Laura (CS): draft customer comms and timeline.

We'll get a mitigation plan back in 30–45 minutes.

Best,
Soojin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Amelia Torres <amelia@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 01:10:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming disconnects causing retry storms

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 11:05 AM -07:00, Amelia Torres <amelia@pulsehealth.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a repeat incident this morning where long-running chat sessions against the Redwood API are disconnecting after ~45–60s of inactivity on the client.

Thanks for the log bundle — I've gone through the trace samples and confirmed two things:
1) The server is closing idle streams at ~60s in a specific load-shedding path when backend queues cross a threshold. That logic was activated by our autoscaler stepping down worker availability during a transient model warm-up.
2) Several client SDKs retry aggressively (linear retry every 500ms for up to 10 attempts) which produces a retry storm when many sessions attempt to reconnect simultaneously.

Proposed immediate mitigations (target: within 2–3 hours):
- Temporarily raise idle disconnect threshold to 120s for session-type routes (configurable flag).
- Turn on server-side heartbeat/ping to active streaming connections every 30s so client sees activity and doesn't retry.
- Add a soft per-session token bucket (burstable) to dampen reconnection rate from a single client.
- Enable model fallback for reopened streams: route to a compatible smaller quantized variant to reduce CPU/GPU pressure.
- Apply circuit-breaker window to reject new stream open attempts with 429 when backend queue depth > X (we'll tune X).

I'll attach the quick-playbook with exact flags and a runbook for Rollback vs Further Action. Aditya and I can push the server flags to Dedicated and Hosted immediately; Private customers will need a patch/deploy window.

Attachments: streaming-resilience-playbook-v1.pdf

I'll coordinate a short maintenance window with PulseHealth ops if you want us to change the thresholds during business hours.

- Priyom
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Intermittent streaming disconnects causing retry storms

1) Please prepare an executive incident summary (impact, ETA for mitigation, customer comms) for me by 09:30 PT.
2) Please include options for a goodwill remediation (service credit or account uplift). Laura, can you draft a short note to Amelia that acknowledges impact and proposes the maintenance window?

On the technical side, Priyom — if the short-term flags are safe to roll (no regression), prioritize the heartbeat and idle-threshold changes first. Please put rollback steps in the summary.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Amelia Torres <amelia@pulsehealth.com>

I'll also have our client SDK team push a patch to add jittered exponential backoff for reconnect attempts (will be a staged rollout). I'll send the exact SDK versions by EOD.

Please confirm ETA and the contact for the maintenance window.

Regards,
Amelia
Director, Integrations — PulseHealth
